description.narrative: The objective of the Project is to foster improved effectiveness of road transport and enhanced efficiency of selected public services, in support of the Borrower's integrated and territorially balanced development agenda. The objective will be achieved through fostering (i) improved accessibility of populations and producers to employment opportunities, services, resources, and markets and enhanced connectivity to the State's territories and productive regions, and (ii) institutional strengthening to contribute to modernize public service delivery and management, promote local economic activities, strengthen environmental management, and improve education.

The objective of the Tocantins Integrated Sustainable Regional Development Project for Brazil is to foster improved effectiveness of road transport and enhanced efficiency of selected public services, in support of the borrower's integrated and territorially balanced development agenda. The project has 3 components. (1) Improving effectiveness of rural transport provision of support component will improve accessibility of the borrower's remote populations and, at the same time, foster regional economic integration and support the borrower's competitiveness and social inclusion agendas. (2) Enhanced efficiency of public services will provide the provision of support for institutional strengthening. (3) Project management component will provide support for project management in connection with the implementation and supervision of the project.

title.narrative: Vehicle-km travelled on State paved roads under good condition
Vehicle-km travelled on State paved roads under good condition

comment.narrative: <p>The value of this indicator is taken into account considering all the roads which are under current CREMA maintenance contracts or recently closed contracts, totalling around 2,200 km. The last traffic count was made in 2018, and due to the pandemic 2020 was postponed until this year. So an assumption is made that of the traffic growth rate of 3% pa. The good condition is defined as IRI<3.5. The indicator overachieved as the traffic grew more than expected and more km of roads were considered compared to the original estimated target (1,500 km). </p>

title.narrative: Concessioned and Operational Municipal Slaughterhouses built related to the project

comment.narrative:
<p>The original indicator was to measure the Increase in volume of meats inspected by the municipal inspection service in the selected municipalities - which was expected to be in 8 Municipalities with one slaughterhouse each. The target at that time was to inspect the total volume of meat produced - as food insecurity was a huge issue - thus target was 100%.</p>

<p>With the last Restructuring, as the slaughterhouses were on hold it was agreed to concesion them and proceed with only the 7 that were partly constructed instead with the 8 envisioned. The 7 slaughterhouses are now concessioned, but still, need to finish the works to become operational. As of closing date of the project, not one is operational. However the slaughterhouses are already part of the Frigotins 25-yearconcession, this is partially achieved and works have resumed now and the first one is expected to open in the next months.  </p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Cooperation agreements on rural road maintenance financing signed between the state and municipal government

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was created as an attempt to create at least 3 inter-municipal consortiums in the road sector for supporting the feeder road maintenance in the municipalities that would be part of those consortiums. As this was not achieved by the time of the last restructuring, the State of Tocantins asked for a change in this indicator, to try to implement cooperation agreements with the 111 municipalities of the State of Tocantins to support the feeder road network under municipal jurisdiction. This was not achieved either and this is one of the main failures of the project, not being able to promote the road maintenance cooperation between municipalities and the State.  </p>

title.narrative: Cooperation agreements on rural road maintenance financing signed between the state and municipal government
Concessioned and Operational Municipal Slaughterhouses built related to the project
Producers which upgrade from subsistence farming to market farming in selected areas

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator is defined as the number of producers who upgrade from subsistence farming to market farming. The number was basedon a program implemented by Ruraltins at the beginning of the project and reached at some point over 150 farmers. Considering that the State of Tocantins did not follow continuously this indicator, it was reached around the year 2019 for good counting the Ruraltins, irrigation work and SEAGRO programs. The latest value is 150 farmers, but the number can be even higher. </p>

title.narrative: Producers which upgrade from subsistence farming to market farming in selected areas

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator measures the kilometres of all rural roads reopened to motorized traffic, rehabilitated, or upgraded under the project. Rural roads are roads functionally classified in various countries below Trunk or Primary, Secondary or Link roads, or sometimes Tertiary roads.  Such roads are often described as rural access, feeder, market, agricultural, irrigation, forestry orcommunity roads. </p>

<p>Typically, rural roads connect small urban centers/towns/settlements of less than 2,000 to 5,000 inhabitants to each other or to higher classes of roads, market towns and urban centers.</p>

<p>In the case of Tocantins this was referred to as the State roads, some of them connecting to even larger urban settlements such as the Capital city, Palmas. The original target was set around 1500 km to be done with CREMA contracts and 2250 km of State roads were finally rehabilitated compared to the original target using CREMA contracts. Additionally, 60 km of unpaved roads were also paved.  </p>

title.narrative: Water management pilot projects implemented in the SoT priority river basins with committees

comment.narrative: <p>River Basin Committees are deliberative stakeholder bodies with decision-making and regulatory powers. The three pilots were prepared by SEMARH but monitoring was loose during the last years of implementation. This one indicator was the first one to be achieved by the project. </p>

title.narrative: Improved public services delivery as measured by substantial achievement of intermediate indicators of Component 2

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator applies to the first indicators for each subcomponent of the Project listed below. Substantial achievement is a) three out of four indicators are substantially achieved at the year of evaluation, where substantial achievement is defined as 75% of the target value of the indicator of the subcomponent. </p>
<p>The components were achieved on all topics with the exceptionof the governance part (subcomponent 2.1), as the maintenance contracts with the municipalities as the main issue were not achieved. Education, agriculture and environmental sub-sectors indicators were all achieved substantially. </p>

title.narrative: Water management pilot projects implemented in the SoT priority river basins with committees
Instruments from the Brazilian Forestry code applied by the State of Tocantins

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was also changed in the last Restructuring from the reduction on illegal deforestation in the Cerrado biome, relative to the 2008-2009 average to the Number of instruments from the Brazilian Forestry code applied by the State of Tocantins with a target of 4 instruments: (Rural Environmental Cadaster; State Secretary and Policy focusing on the topic; monitoring of illegal deforestation and wildfires; natural capital tool elaborated) and a baseline was 0 at the beginning of the project. The 4 instruments were established successfully, therefore it was achieved. </p>

title.narrative: Improved public services delivery as measured by substantial achievement of intermediate indicators of Component 2
Instruments from the Brazilian Forestry code applied by the State of Tocantins
Agencies with implemented results agreements between the secretaries and responsible units

comment.narrative:
<p>Management adopted by the staff of the Beneficiary institutions is subject to the implementation of results-based management (SEPLAN, SEINFRA, SEMARH, SEAGRO, SEDUC).</p>
<p>This indicator was achieved with the support of consultancies to implement this management. </p>

title.narrative: Agencies with implemented results agreements between the secretaries and responsible units
Extension of municipal roads with all-season accessibility

comment.narrative: <p>The project has achieved this target despite having some pending actions left at project closing on the feeder road network, with less than 100 interventions pending of more than 1600 planned on the feeder network. The amount of feeder road kilometres that are accessible all year round has therefore achieved the target.  </p>

Municipal Education Plans (with Early Childhood Education (ECE) component) agreed with municipalities
Municipal Education Plans (with Early Childhood Education (ECE) component) agreed with municipalities

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was achieved in 2018 with having each of the Municipalities with Schools of the Program submitted to the Bank itsfinalized plans signed by State and Municipal government. In total the Municipalities implemented the plan with the renovated schools as well. </p>

title.narrative: Reduction of dropout rate in 7 pilot state schools identified by the the SoT
Reduction of dropout rate in 7 pilot state schools identified by the the SoT

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator measures the average dropout rate across entire schools of the Program. Having the data available was difficult asshool-wide indicators have a lot of variability as well. The data of the last year showed a large reduction in the dropout rate as a result of the online classes that counted all the children in school age to be participating in lessons, so indicator was achievedbut this has to be put on question as a result of the pandemic impact. Actually, before the pandemic the indicator progress was around 7 percent. </p>

title.narrative: Teachers in state system trained in 7 schools identified by the SoT

comment.narrative: <p>To qualify, the training must include at least 40 hours of face-to-face training and at least 4 in-class follow-up visits for each professor. Indicator is calculated as number trained (as above), divided by total state-employed teachers in pilot schools. The original target was 90 percent, but this was not achieved as training stopped when COVID pandemic reached the State in 2020, therefore 15 percent of teachers were left without completing the training. </p>

title.narrative: Teachers in state system trained in 7 schools identified by the SoT
Average time to concession environmental licensing for complex State road activities with environmental impact
Average time to concession environmental licensing for complex State road activities with environmental impact

comment.narrative:
<p>The environmental licensing average time refers to the time spent within the Naturatins, since the license is required until the license is issued, except for downtime by backlogs of the entrepreneur (environmental assessments, studies, action plans, etc.). It is the Sum of the required time in days to concede (or deny) a license divided by the number of licenses issued by Naturatins officrs each year, regarding complex road activities.</p>
<p>It was achieved at the end. During some time, the indicator was even at 29 days. </p>

title.narrative: Share of rural population with access to an all-season road

comment.narrative:
<p>This indicator measures the percentage of rural people in the project area who live within 2 kilometres (typically equivalent to a 20-minute walk) of an all-season road.  This indicator is also known as Rural Access Index (RAI). This indicator also considrs that an all-season road is motorable all year by the prevailing means of rural transport (often a pick-up or a truck which does not have a four-wheel drive), though predictable interruptions of short duration during inclement weather (e.g. heavy rainfall) are acceptable, particularly on low volume roads. </p>
<p>Thanks to the construction of works on feeder and rural roads by the project, the population in the Western part of the Tocantins State (the focus area of the project) has currently access to all-season roads. Even in areas where the roads were not fully built by project closing, roads were elevated and thus passable, contributing to the indicator. Almost the whole population of the Western part of the State has now access to jobs and services all year round. This also was over achieved compared to the original target of 92 percent of the population. </p>

title.narrative: Percentage of CREMA State road network in good condition

comment.narrative: <p>The Road network considered is the one either under current CREMA or recently closed contracts, totalling 2,200 km or almost 1/2 of the total state paved road network. A good condition is defined as IRI<3.5. </p>
